Nex Clone needs to create an Android work profile where cloned apps run separately from the originals.

Nex Clone will create an Android work profile right away as the space for apps you install. A system consent screen will appear; follow its steps.\n\nApps in the work profile use data and accounts separate from the original app. Deleting the work profile deletes all their data.

Run two accounts of the same app at once, such as WhatsApp, Instagram or games, with separate data.

Nex Clone uses Android’s built-in work profile, not a virtual machine. That means clones show a briefcase badge and also appear in your phone launcher, their data is separate from the original app, and App lock and Private Space only apply when opening through Nex Clone or its shortcuts. Deleting the work profile deletes the data of all clones.

Nex Clone creates Android’s built-in work profile. Apps you clone are installed again in that profile with separate data and accounts, so you can sign in with a second account. Cloned apps are opened through Nex Clone.
Why is there a briefcase badge and duplicate apps in my launcher?
Android marks work-profile apps with a briefcase badge and shows them in the launcher too. This is normal and cannot be hidden by an app.
Cloned app notifications do not appear.
Open User center, Notification management, then pick the app. Also make sure the work profile is not paused in your phone settings.
Can a clone use the original app’s data?
No. Work-profile data is separate from the main profile. That is what keeps accounts and data isolated.
Most can. Apps that refuse to run in a work profile, or need services missing from the profile, may fail. Try One-key repair if a clone misbehaves.
